slides.0.title: The regulatory system: DAC, Ried and ÖTW
slides.0.subtitle: From Landwein to Riedenwein
slides.1.title: The quality pyramid
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Landwein and Qualitätswein
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Landwein needs at least 14 KMW and Qualitätswein at least 15 KMW; above Qualitätswein come Kabinett and the Prädikat levels
slides.1.highlights.1.title: The DAC idea
slides.1.highlights.1.content: DAC (Districtus Austriae Controllatus) is regionally typical Qualitätswein: set varieties, style and minimum alcohol, with the region name rather than the variety on the label
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Three tiers
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Most DACs follow a geographic pyramid: Gebietswein (region) → Ortswein (village) → Riedenwein (single vineyard)
slides.1.content: DAC writes style into law, while Prädikat looks at sugar.
slides.2.title: Klassik and Reserve
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Klassik
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A lighter, fruit-driven style; most DACs set a minimum around 12% abv (it varies by DAC)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Reserve
slides.2.highlights.1.content: A more concentrated, ageworthy style, typically at least 13% abv; Weinviertel, for example, has had Reserve since the 2009 vintage
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Labelling principle
slides.2.highlights.2.content: DAC wines carry the region name; wines that fall outside the DAC rules are labelled as ordinary Qualitätswein with the variety
slides.2.content: Thresholds differ by DAC, so check each region before an exam.
slides.3.title: Ried and the ÖTW
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Ried
slides.3.highlights.0.content: A Ried is a named single-vineyard site, shown on the label as Ried plus its name
slides.3.highlights.1.title: The ÖTW
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The Österreichische Traditionsweingüter was founded in 1992; its member estates classify Rieden themselves
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Erste Lage
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The ÖTW Erste Lage covers dry Grüner Veltliner and Riesling in Kamptal, Kremstal, Traisental and Wagram, later joined by Wien and Carnuntum (Carnuntum's classification was still pending at the time)
slides.3.content: The ÖTW is a private association, not a statutory classification; the Riedenwein tier within each DAC is the legal one.
What does a DAC label normally show?
DAC is regionally typical Qualitätswein, with the region name at the core of the label.
In which year was the ÖTW founded?
The ÖTW was founded in 1992 by estates along the Danube.
C. A type of oak cask
D. A collective name for a region
A Ried is a single vineyard shown on the label as Ried plus its name.
